content: E2E key recovery: passkeys/PRF give a deterministic 32-byte secret per credential, no built-in recovery; losing all credentials = data loss; recoverable designs widen attack surface. Standard pattern: random master key wrapped separately per passkey and by a one-time recovery code; treat PRF output as IKM through a KDF; platform PRF support is uneven. FTC v. Zoom (2020): 'end-to-end encrypted' means not even the provider can read; marketing it while servers hold keys is deceptive.
